text:
maria_cust: hey team, our app started seeing a big latency jump after we switched to the new model variant yesterday (~11:30 UTC). p99 for completions on /v1/generate jumped from ~420ms to ~1.8s. p95 up to ~900ms. All requests use long_context=true and max_tokens=1024. can you take a look?

jamie_support: hi Maria, sorry about that :frowning: can you paste a sample request id or timestamp so we can correlate? any errors in response body or just slow?

maria_cust: no errors, just slower responses. sample request id: req_20260314_1432_07, timestamp 2026-03-14T11:32:07Z. payload attached (we're sending a 6k token prompt, plus 1k max_tokens).

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-314-tokenizer-latency (severity: medium). assigned to jamie_support.

jamie_support: thanks. quick check of infra - nothing obvious on capacity side, no queued GPUs. forwarding to ML/runtime for profiling. @sana_ml @liam_runtime can you eyeball p95/p99 traces?

sana_ml: looking at traces now. I can see a sharp increase in self-attention kernel times for the new model variant (redwood-xt-4k-tokenizer v2). p99 step_time for tokenization+kv_cache ops spiked. baseline model (redwood-xt-4k v1) doesn't show this.

liam_runtime: interesting — related to tokenizer change? We deployed a tokenizer update that changed split behavior for certain whitespace/punctuation sequences. That can make sequence length in tokens > characters significantly for some payloads. If actual tokenized length jumped from 6k->9k tokens, KV-cache and attention cost would blow up.

sana_ml: confirm. I ran local tokenization for Maria's sample prompt with new tokenizer binary: tokens=9124. with v1 tokenizer tokens=6142. attention cost scales ~O(seq^2) for some backends when KV caching not used efficiently for long contexts. This explains p99 blowup.

maria_cust: so this is because the tokenizer split changed? we didn't change inputs. we rely on model compat behavior.

jamie_support: short answer yes. longer: tokenizer variant associated with the model changed tokenization rules which increased token counts for certain unicode sequences. we should have a compatibility note, but immediate mitigation steps below.

liam_runtime: mitigation options (short-term):
- pin customers to older tokenizer/model variant (redwood-xt-4k@v1) via `model_override` on the route.
- enable server-side prefix/KV caching for long_context where feasible (reduces recompute for repeated prefixes).
- autoscale burst capacity temporarily to absorb p99 until we roll out a fix.
- lower max_tokens or set `truncate=true` for clients where acceptable.

jamie_support: for Maria specifically, I can pin your workspace to redwood-xt-4k@v1 immediately. Maria, want me to do that?

maria_cust: yes please do that asap. also would like a timeline for a permanent fix - our customers are hitting timeouts.

sana_ml: permanent fix options:
1) revert tokenizer changes for the problematic rules and release v2.1 with conservative splits.
2) add an opt-in compatibility flag in the model metadata so tokenizer v2 preserves legacy splits for `compat=legacy` routes.
3) add server-side token count guard (reject or warn if tokenized length > X) and return structured error with suggested actions.

liam_runtime: engineering notes: we also discovered a regression in the KV-cache allocator that causes memory churn when tokenized_length > 8k on some GPU kernels, which degraded throughput further. Need a small runtime patch to preallocate better and avoid per-step realloc. I can push a hotfix to staging.

jamie_support: next steps I'm taking now:
- pin Maria to v1 variant (done) -> please confirm after 2 deploy cycles.
- notify CS and set customer-facing status update.
- create ticket for ML/runtime to triage tokenizer + KV patch: TICKET-2026-314-TOKPATCH (assign to sana/liam)

ops-bot: redeploy request: redeploy model redwood-xt-4k@v1 to customer workspace maria_cust (req 1762006700) queued.

maria_cust: confirmed latency dropped back to p99 ~480ms after pin. thanks.

sana_ml: creating PR to revert the aggressive split rule and adding a regression test with Maria's prompt to ensure token counts stay within expected band. PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2345 (WIP). Will include a tokenizer fuzz test that checks edge unicode sequences.

liam_runtime: I pushed a runtime prealloc hotfix to staging (build 2026.03.14-rtf1). Rolling to canary now. If canary is healthy, will promote to prod tonight. This should cut the extra churn for >8k tokens even if tokenizer changes persist.

jamie_support: good. I'll keep this thread updated. Also flagging for docs: we need to call out tokenizer compatibility in model release notes and provide `compat` option in model metadata.

maria_cust: appreciate the quick turnaround. can you also send a small FAQ for our SREs to tweak retries/timeouts while the fix lands?

jamie_support: sure — will post remediation steps in #support-docs and paste a short checklist here in 30m.

sana_ml: summary for the ticket: root cause = tokenizer split rule change increased tokenized length for certain inputs -> quadratic attention cost + runtime KV allocator churn -> p95/p99 regression. mitigations = pin to prior model variant, rollback/tweak tokenizer rules, runtime prealloc hotfix, guard warnings for high token counts.

liam_runtime: logging snippet used to investigate:```
TRACE 2026-03-14T11:33:12Z model=redwood-xt-4k-tokenizer_v2 req=req_20260314_1432_07 tokenized_len=9124 attn_step_ms=1245 kv_alloc_retries=8 gpu_mem_peak=12.3G
TRACE 2026-03-14T11:33:13Z model=redwood-xt-4k_v1 req=req_20260314_1432_07 tokenized_len=6142 attn_step_ms=412 kv_alloc_retries=0 gpu_mem_peak=8.9G
```

jamie_support: cc @product to consider model release checklist update. I'll close the incident once PR and runtime patch are merged and canary->prod done.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-314-tokenizer-latency status updated: remediation in progress.

maria_cust: thanks all, will monitor.

jamie_support: closing loop: patch merged (PR 2345), runtime hotfix promoted to prod at 2026-03-14T23:45Z. we rolled tokenizer v2.1 with conservative split rules and added compatibility flag. Please re-open if you see any recurrence. :thumbsup:
